title.narrative: Humanitarian Capacity Strengthening Project for SOCOAC (April 16 - March 18)

description.narrative:
The northern part of the North Kivu Province in DRC has been marked by recurring insecurity due to armed groups attacks namely from famous Ugandan rebels known under ADF-NALU acronym. DRC authorities has declared them to be a terrorist group which should deserve close international community attention. This said, SOCOAC was created on a development base intending to federate local farmers in a region where soil is fertile and people may produce enough food for their families and even for market. They have progressively moved to humanitarian since a few years ago and developed partnership with CAFOD and others including FAO, Care International, etc.
SOCOAC was part of the Phase One of the Humanitarian Capacity Development programme (HCD), the only non-faith based organisation within the portfolio in the West-Africa and Great Lakes (WAGL). In our DRC Strategy for the HCD, we recalled the importance of continued support to existing partners mostly for consolidating achievements and ensure we prepare consciously and bilaterally an exist process. Meanwhile, since the start of Phase Two in April 2016, the HCD framework was revised to adapt to new trends in humanitarian. As a consequence, some of almost completed capacity where reassessed to low score which is normal given the new lenses used. However, SOCOAC has improved continuously its humanitarian work through providing assistance to affected community in the Beni territory thanks to START fund in particular. The structure is still weak as that is the case for most of national organisations because of institutional funding issue.
Earlier November 2016, a self-assessment was conducted with their team in Beni with around 20 staffs participating. The following result were considered to be a basis for their new capacity strengthening plan until mars 2018. There is a need to: a) Improve managerial capacities for senior staff in alignment to the Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS) b) Develop a comprehensive strategy for resources mobilization. . c) Draw up their communication policy focused on the humanitarian context in Beni territory. d) Develop policies for better staff management and its performance development. e) Acquire an accounting software and adapt to OHADA system in accordance with new requirement in the DRC. f) Improve capacity in humanitarian programming based on the CHS g) Systematize the monitoring and learning practices.
In relation with the staff turnover which is a consequence of the lack of institutional funds, internal discussion in the DRC team concluded that additional funds of 5,000 £ from another CAFOD source will be allocated to SOCOAC to complement the 5,000 £ dedicated by the HCD. The extra amount from the DRC country budget will cover their Emergency Programme Assistant costs.
